title: Bronco (sixth generation)
verdict: Ford spent 25 years working out how to beat the Wrangler and mostly managed it: a boxy, doors-off, body-on-frame 4x4 whose independent front suspension rides well, plus a factory 35-inch package that ends most tire arguments. Early trucks had their teething troubles in the roof and on the recall list, so buy one with the VIN check done.

paragraphs: Twenty-five years after the last [[bronco/full-size|full-size Bronco]], the name came back because of a factory. In Ford's 2016 contract talks with the UAW, Michigan Assembly in Wayne was set to lose the Focus and C-Max. Instead it was retooled for a new North American Ranger and, since one truck wouldn't fill the plant, a new Bronco. Ford confirmed it at the 2017 Detroit show, showed it on July 13, 2020 after pandemic delays, and built the first customer trucks on June 14, 2021, in the same plant as the previous five generations. Its target was obvious: the [[jeep/jl|Wrangler JL]] and [[jeep/jl-unlimited|JL Unlimited]], in both two- and four-door form.

story.heading: HOW IT'S BUILT
paragraphs: Underneath is Ford's T6 body-on-frame platform, shared with the Ranger. Unlike the Jeep, the front suspension is independent, with twin A-arms. The rear has a solid axle on five links and coilovers, and Ford claimed 17 percent more front wheel travel and 10 percent more rear travel than the Wrangler. Styling borrows from the 1966–77 [[bronco/early-bronco|first Bronco]]; the design chief's own 1976 truck was digitally scanned for reference. The doors are frameless and come off with one bolt per hinge. The mirrors stay behind on the cowl, and the doors can ride in protective bags in the cargo area.

Two engines launched it. The 2.3 EcoBoost four makes 300 hp and 325 lb-ft and the 2.7 twin-turbo V6 330 hp and 415 lb-ft, both on premium fuel and both well above Ford's original estimates. The four is offered with a Getrag seven-speed manual, which is really a six-speed plus a crawler gear marked 'C', or Ford's 10-speed automatic. The V6 is automatic-only. Two transfer cases were offered: a part-time unit with a 2.72:1 low range, and an advanced one with a full-time 4A mode and a 3.06:1 low range. Ford quoted a 95:1 crawl ratio for the manual with the crawler gear.

story.heading: SASQUATCH, HOSS AND THE RAPTOR
paragraphs: The Sasquatch package is the headline option: 315/70R17 tires (35 inches) on +30 mm-offset wheels, 4.7 axle gears, a mild lift, and the Bilstein dampers and sway-bar disconnect of the off-road trims. On 35s, MotorTrend measured 11.6 inches of ground clearance and approach, departure and breakover angles of 43.2, 37.2 and 29.0 degrees for the two-door. Ford calls its suspension packages HOSS. Badlands trucks get position-sensitive Bilstein dampers and a hydraulic front anti-roll-bar disconnect that reconnects itself at speed. The Wildtrak's HOSS 3.0 uses Fox dampers. For 2025, Badlands buyers could add full HOSS 3.0, with Fox 2.5-inch internal-bypass shocks, the Raptor's severe-duty steering rack and stronger tie rods.

Then there's the Raptor, added for 2022 as a four-door only. It has a 3.0-liter twin-turbo V6 with 418 hp and 440 lb-ft, Fox suspension, 37-inch tires, 13.1 inches of ground clearance, F-150 Raptor brakes and a body widened to 85.7 inches. It gets 'FORD' across the grille instead of 'BRONCO' and is rated to tow 4,500 lb, 1,000 lb more than the standard Bronco. The cost is fuel: the EPA rates a 2023 Raptor at 15 mpg combined.

story.heading: TWO DOORS OR FOUR
paragraphs: The two-door rides on a 100.4-inch wheelbase and is 174.8 inches long. MotorTrend noted it is 6.9 inches longer than a two-door Wrangler on a 3.6-inch-longer wheelbase, and much roomier inside. The four-door stretches to 116.1 inches between the axles and about 190 inches overall. That costs breakover angle (26.3 degrees against 29.0 on 35s), and the four-door weighs up to about 400 lb more, but it has the bigger fuel tank (21.1 gallons against 17.4) and, at launch, the soft-top option, and the Raptor was built only as a four-door. Both come with removable roofs; the standard hardtop is molded in black or white, and a painted top arrived later.

story.heading: TEETHING TROUBLES
paragraphs: Demand was huge: Ford sold 117,057 in the US in 2022 and 146,007 in 2025. Early trucks had problems. In August 2021, Ford began replacing molded-in-color hardtops whose finish crazed and delaminated, and a 2026 recall covers 2021–22 roof panels that can separate on the road. Some 2021–22 2.7 V6s can break intake valves. Bilstein rear shocks on 2021–24 trucks can corrode until the reservoir detaches. A service bulletin covers seven-speed manuals that grind. By September 2026, Jalopnik counted about 20 recalls since launch. Buy a sixth-gen Bronco on its VIN history.

callout.label: SIDEBAR · THE MILLION-DOLLAR FIRST EDITION
callout.title: VIN 1 and a badly chosen date
paragraphs: Ford unintentionally first scheduled the reveal for July 9, 2020, O.J. Simpson's birthday, then moved it to July 13. On March 27, 2021, the first production Bronco, a First Edition, sold at Barrett-Jackson in Scottsdale for $1,075,000, with the money going to a forest-conservation charity Ford helped set up.

The First Edition combined Badlands hardware with Wildtrak looks and the Outer Banks interior. MotorTrend reported a 3,500-unit run at the reveal, and Ford later built more because of demand. One sold on Bring a Trailer in August 2026 for $40,810.

engineering_intro: The Bronco is a body-on-frame Ranger derivative with a removable roof and doors. It has independent front suspension, a coil-sprung solid rear axle and Dana axles, with electronic lockers optional front and rear. Off-road settings are chosen with a dial and the G.O.A.T. ('Goes Over Any Type of Terrain') drive modes, not a second lever.

engineering.v: Ladder frame, Ford T6 (U725) · 100.4 / 116.1 in wheelbase
engineering.note: Shared with the Ranger; built at Michigan Assembly, Wayne, Michigan, and for China by Jiangling Ford in Nanchang from 2024.
Badlands and Sasquatch add a hydraulic front sway-bar disconnect that reconnects above about 20 mph.
MotorTrend describes trailing links and a Panhard rod; electronic locker available.
Electric shift on both; Ford quoted a 95:1 crawl ratio with the manual's crawler gear.

buying_checks.head: Run the VIN before anything else
buying_checks.body: There are many open-recall possibilities. The big ones are the 2.7 intake valves (24V-635), the rear shock reservoirs (25V-025), 2021–22 molded-in-color roof panels (26V-299, remedy expected November 2026), engine-bay wiring (26V-468), fender flares (26V-403) and, on 2024–25 trucks, loose front control-arm and ball-joint fasteners (24V-770, 25V-260, 25V-308, 25V-310). Get a printout from NHTSA's VIN lookup.

buying_checks.head: Look hard at the hardtop
buying_checks.body: Molded-in-color tops were standard on 2021–23 trucks and most 2024s. Crazing or delamination means the top needs replacing: Ford's August 2021 program fitted 'MIC 2.0' tops, and some owners are on their third or fourth. Painted tops arrived for 2025. Check the headliner and seals for leaks and make sure every panel latches.

buying_checks.head: 2.7 V6: ask about the engine test
buying_checks.body: Recall 24V-635 covers 2021–22 2.7 and 3.0 Nano EcoBoost engines whose intake valves can break. Dealers run an engine cycle test and replace the engine if needed. Bronco Nation names V6s built from May 1 to October 31, 2021 as the bad batch. Get proof the test was done.

buying_checks.head: Rear shocks on Badlands and Sasquatch
buying_checks.body: Bilstein rear shocks on trucks built from September 23, 2020 to July 23, 2024 can corrode until the external reservoir detaches (25V-025). Look at the reservoirs and their mounts and confirm the replacement was done.

buying_checks.head: Drive the manual through every gear
buying_checks.body: On 2021–23 seven-speed trucks, a scraping noise in neutral, first or second is the subject of a Ford service bulletin. Check for clean engagement of the crawler gear and reverse.

buying_checks.head: Steering and tie rods on modified trucks
buying_checks.body: Owners have reported tie rods failing during hard off-road use, usually on lifted trucks with bigger tires. Inspect the inner and outer tie rods for bends. The 2023 Wildtrak and 2022 Raptor had a steering-gear recall (23V-155) for internal damage that could lock the wheel.

buying_checks.head: Was it flat-towed?
buying_checks.body: 2021–22 trucks had a neutral-tow problem: Ford issued a temporary fix in May 2022 and an over-the-air update by March 2023. Bronco Nation warns that flat-tow damage to the transmission can be hard to get covered under warranty, so ask how the truck traveled behind a motorhome.

buying_checks.head: Is it a real Sasquatch?
buying_checks.body: Factory Sasquatch trucks have 315/70R17 tires on 17x8.5, +30 mm wheels and 4.7 gears. A truck that only has aftermarket 35s may still have the original gearing and +55 mm wheels. Check the window sticker or the build data.

repairs.title: Rear shock reservoir corrosion (Bilstein, HOSS 2.0)
repairs.cost: Free under recall 25V-025 on eligible trucks
repairs.symptoms: Rusty or swollen reservoir bodies on the rear shocks, a reservoir hanging by its hose, oil on the shock body, or a bouncy rear end.
repairs.fix: Check the VIN first: Ford's remedy for 2021–24 Badlands and Sasquatch trucks built from September 23, 2020 to July 23, 2024 is free rear shock replacement (Ford campaign 25S01; owner letters went out in August 2025). On an out-of-scope or modified truck, support the axle on a jack, unbolt the upper and lower shock mounts and the reservoir clamp, fit the new shocks, and torque at ride height. Rinse road salt off the reservoirs in winter.
repairs.tools: Jack and stands · sockets · torque wrench.

repairs.title: Hardtop crazing, delamination and leaks
repairs.cost: Covered by Ford's program and recall on eligible tops; Bronco Nation cites out-of-warranty figures of $2,000 to $5,000+
repairs.symptoms: Spider-web crazing or bubbling in the outer skin of a molded-in-color top, water dripping at panel joints, or a roof panel that won't latch flush.
repairs.fix: Look over every panel in daylight for crazing and delamination. Affected 2021-on tops were replaced with MIC 2.0 tops under Ford's August 2021 customer-satisfaction program, and recall 26V-299 (2021–22) covers roof panels whose outer skin can separate on the road; owners were notified in May 2026, and the remedy is expected in November 2026. For leaks, remove each panel, clean the seals and sealing faces, check that no seal is pinched or folded, and refit, latching the panels in the order the owner's manual shows.
repairs.tools: Mild soap and water · seal conditioner · the factory panel bags for storage.

parts.name: ExtremeTerrain — Bronco hard and soft top replacement parts

repairs.title: Upgrade or replace tie rods
repairs.symptoms: A bent tie rod after a hard hit on the trail, toe out of spec, the steering wheel off-center, or a tie rod that has failed outright on a lifted truck with big tires.
repairs.fix: Ford's own answer was stronger hardware. The 2024 Badlands and Sasquatch got the Wildtrak's HOSS 3.0 steering gear, and the 2025 HOSS 3.0 option added upgraded inner and outer tie rods with the Raptor's severe-duty rack. To replace a tie rod, mark or count the turns on the old outer end, separate it from the knuckle, unscrew the inner rod from the rack under the boot, fit the new parts to the same length and torque them, then get an alignment.
repairs.tools: Tie-rod separator · inner tie-rod tool · torque wrench · tape measure.

parts.name: ExtremeTerrain — Bronco tie rods, ends and ball joints

repairs.title: Fit 35s to a non-Sasquatch Bronco
repairs.time: A weekend with a level kit
repairs.cost: Wheels, tires and a level kit; regearing extra
repairs.symptoms: You want 35s, but your truck has +55 mm wheels and stock height.
repairs.fix: Performance Plus Tire's guide splits it by tire width. A 285/75R17 (about 33.8 in) fits stock wheels and suspension without rubbing. Narrow 35s (35x10.50R17 or 35x11.50R17) fit factory 17-inch wheels once the front crash bars come off, usually with a small 1.25–1.5-inch level. Full-width 35x12.50R17s need about +30 mm wheels, high-clearance flares and roughly 1.5–2 inches of lift. Afterwards, recalibrate the speedometer (35s read about 7% slow) and get an alignment. Regearing is optional: the Sasquatch uses 4.7s, and the guide says 4.46s work fine for many owners.
repairs.tools: Jack and stands · spring compressor or pre-assembled coilovers · torque wrench · speedometer calibration tool.

parts.name: ExtremeTerrain — Bronco ring and pinion gears

repairs.title: Check the front suspension fasteners (2024–25)
repairs.cost: Free under recall where it applies
repairs.symptoms: A clunk from the front end, or nothing at all: a missing or loose upper ball-joint nut or lower control-arm bolt may give no warning before the arm separates.
repairs.fix: Four campaigns cover this (24V-770, 25V-260, 25V-310 and 25V-308). For 25V-260 and 25V-308, Ford told owners not to drive the truck until it was repaired. The remedy is to inspect and, if needed, tighten or replace the fasteners, ball joint and knuckle. On any lifted or modified truck, check the torque on the upper ball-joint nuts and the lower control-arm pivot bolts after installation and again after the first trail run.
repairs.tools: Torque wrench · sockets · jack and stands.

parts.name: ExtremeTerrain — Bronco control arms and accessories
Control arms and ball joints, 2024 Bronco

repairs.title: Re-secure loose fender flares
repairs.symptoms: A flare that flaps, gaps or rattles at speed, or missing clips along its edge.
repairs.fix: Recall 26V-403 covers 2022–26 Broncos whose fender flares may not be properly secured and can come off; dealers inspect and repair or replace them. Between visits, check every flare fastener after washing or trail use, especially on trucks whose owners have removed the flares for bigger tires and refitted them.
repairs.tools: Trim tools · Torx and socket set.

repairs.title: Protect the engine-bay wiring
repairs.symptoms: Chafed or melted insulation on the harness in the engine bay, intermittent electrical faults, or a burning smell.
repairs.fix: Recall 26V-468 covers 2021–26 Broncos and Bronco Raptors whose engine-compartment harness can be damaged and short-circuit; dealers add protective sheathing. Ford phased the campaign: 2026 Raptors first, then 2021–25 Raptors, then all other Broncos from about September 2026. Until it's done, look along the harness for chafe points and keep added wiring for lights and accessories well clear of it.
repairs.tools: Flashlight · split loom and zip ties for your own accessory wiring.

faq.q: What's the biggest tire I can fit without a lift?
faq.a: On stock wheels and suspension, a 285/75R17 (about 33.8 in) with no rubbing reported. Narrow 35s (35x10.50R17 or 35x11.50R17) fit factory 17s once the front crash bars are removed, usually with a small level of 1.25–1.5 in. Full-width 35x12.50R17s need about +30 mm wheels, high-clearance flares and roughly 1.5–2 in of lift. The factory way to get 35s is the Sasquatch package (315/70R17); the Raptor runs 37s.

The 2.3 four (300 hp, 325 lb-ft) is the only engine with the manual and the more economical one: the EPA rates a 2021 at 21 mpg combined, against 19 for the 2.7. The 2.7 V6 (330 hp, 415 lb-ft) is automatic-only, and 2021–22 versions are covered by the intake-valve recall. Both ratings are on premium fuel; on regular, Ford quotes 275 and 315 hp.

faq.q: Is the seven-speed manual really a seven-speed?
faq.a: Not quite. It's a Getrag six-speed with an extra crawler gear marked 'C', down and left of reverse in a dog-leg. It's for rock crawling and steep ramps, and with the advanced transfer case Ford quoted a 95:1 crawl ratio. About 15% of early buyers chose it.

faq.q: Is the Sasquatch package worth it?
faq.a: If you off-road, yes. You get 35-inch tires, 4.7 gears, position-sensitive Bilstein dampers, the sway-bar disconnect, ground clearance up to 11.6 in and much better angles. The EPA cost is real: a 2021 2.3 automatic Sasquatch is rated 18 mpg combined against 21 for the standard truck. Adding the same parts later costs more than the package.
3,500 lb for the standard Bronco, the same as a Wrangler. The Bronco Raptor is rated at 4,500 lb.

The two-door (100.4 in wheelbase) is shorter, lighter and has the better breakover angle (29.0° against 26.3° on 35s). The four-door (116.1 in) has the rear doors, more cargo room, a 21.1-gallon tank instead of 17.4, offered the soft top at launch, and is the only body offered as a Raptor.

faq.q: How do the doors and roof come off?
faq.a: Lower the window, slip on the door bag, unplug the connector and remove one bolt from each hinge. The doors are frameless and the mirrors stay on the cowl. The two roof panels over the front seats release with quarter-turn latches and stow on board in bags. On four-doors a third panel over the rear seat also comes off but doesn't stow on board, and the remaining rear section is small enough to handle easily.

faq.q: Which years should I buy or avoid?
faq.a: 2021–22 trucks have the most recalls, including the 2.7 valves, roof panels and early camera software. Later trucks benefit from fixes: MIC 2.0 tops, a painted-top option from 2025, the HOSS 3.0 steering gear on 2024 Badlands and Sasquatch, and a full HOSS 3.0 option for 2025. But 2024–25 trucks have their own front-suspension fastener recalls, so check any year's VIN.

faq.q: What oil does it take, and how much?
faq.a: SAE 5W-30 synthetic blend meeting WSS-M2C961-A1. The 2.3 takes 6.2 qt with the filter (Motorcraft FL-910-S). The 2.7 is listed at 7 qt (FL-2062-A), but owners on Bob Is The Oil Guy report a later Ford bulletin giving 6 qt for a drain and fill, so fill to the dipstick. The 10-speed takes Mercon ULV and the transfer case Mercon LV.

So far Consumer Reports calls it average, according to Jalopnik, which counted about 20 recalls by September 2026. Most problems were in the 2021–22 trucks: hardtops, 2.7 valves, rear shocks, manual-transmission noise. Bronco Nation's view is that tie-rod failures are rarer than the internet suggests and usually involve lifts, big tires or hard driving.

faq.q: What's different about the Bronco Raptor?
faq.a: It has a 3.0 twin-turbo V6 (418 hp), Fox suspension, 37-inch tires, a body 85.7 in wide, 13.1 in of ground clearance, F-150 Raptor brakes, a reinforced bumper and frame, and 'FORD' on the grille. It's four-door only, tows 4,500 lb and the EPA rates a 2023 at 15 mpg combined.

mods.why: A 1.25–2-inch level makes room for 35s on non-Sasquatch trucks. Bigger lifts need attention to CV angles and steering.
Bigger tires load up the tie rods. Ford's own HOSS 3.0 parts and aftermarket heavy-duty rods are the common fix.

who.name: ExtremeTerrain — Bronco tie rods and ball joints

mods.why: Wheels with about +30 mm offset clear full-width 35s, and 4.46 or 4.7 gears restore the Sasquatch's gearing.
The factory skid plates cover the essentials. A steel bumper, rock rails and extra skids are what you add before the rocks find the rest.
Ford's modular steel bumper is designed to take a winch; fit real recovery points before you need them.
Replacement seals, hardtop parts, soft tops and tube doors fix the Bronco's two weak spots: water and wind.
